citations.claim: initial state starts clear of wall with 0.56 gap
after one step body is essentially touching wall surface, gap 0.023
first violating step: body overlaps wall 0 by 0.228, centre inside expanded wall region
y at violating step places circle overlapping thin wall slab

counterfactual.change: reduced dt from 0.012166783887663915 to 0.001 with all else identical; finer integration resolves the thin-wall impact and no violation occurs

explanation: High-speed (~53 m/s) body strikes thin (0.2 thick) wall. Per-step displacement ~0.6 exceeds wall thickness plus correction budget, so discrete impulse plus positional correction at dt=0.01216 fails to eject the circle; by step 2 it sits 0.228 deep in overlap. Reducing dt alone removes the failure, pointing to inadequate continuous collision / substep resolution for fast vs thin-wall impacts.
vision_note: The red circle approaches the right tip of the thin horizontal wall from above and makes contact. By step 2 it sits embedded overlapping the wall end instead of bouncing off.
